blocks.body:
Requirements

Blender 5.2. Compatibility is not guaranteed on earlier versions.

Installation/Update

To install or update, find top left the Edit menu, then select “Preferences…”

Then go in “Get Extensions” and find the down arrow top right, then select ”Install from Disk…“

Then locate and select the downloaded NeverDestruct Zip file, and press “Install from Disk”

chapters.title: General overview of the modifier stack

blocks.body:
Basic interactions

You will find all new modifiers directly in the add modifier panel, just like any regular modifier, they're displayed above the others as a quick way to access them.

In addition to new modifiers, the addon adds a Base mesh layer as well that sits above all the modifiers.

Most new modifiers (such as Edit poly, Edit mesh, Shape keys or Weight Map) have a toggle to activate them, activating them allows you to interact with the mesh in this modifier specifically.

Activating a modifier that doesn’t support modifying the mesh (such as Weight Map or Shape Keys) will automatically warn you that you are interacting in a layer that doesn’t support topology edits, your edits will not be stored.

 

Base Mesh

This represents the most upstream mesh state, this is the default blender way, this modifies the mesh before any modifier. Since using the new modifiers is totally optional, you retain total access to modifying the mesh there. Applying modifiers will also push them to the base mesh layer (for example, base mesh + edit poly, applying edit poly will make base mesh become what edit poly was).

 

Edit Poly and Edit Mesh

Those are the mesh editing modifiers, however their use and features are very different:

Edit poly is the modifier with the full replay system, the journal system, the safety features and it is the most non destructive modifier. Edit poly is capable of saving all changes, topology, uv edits, vertex groups and shapekeys, all are saved within that layer. 

Edit mesh is a lightweight mesh editing modifier, it retains some level of non destructiveness, but not to the extent of Edit poly. 

Both modifiers store their edits as relative to whatever is arriving in the modifier, meaning they're technically independent, nothing stops you from changing the topology above the layer, whether using another mesh editing modifier or anything else (geometry nodes, displacements...).

Shape Keys and Weight Map

These are dedicated modifiers to purely save shape keys and weight map changes, no topology edits can be stored in these modifiers, and attempting to make topology edits will display a warning.

FFD and Symmetry

FFD is a wrapper for the lattice modifier already available in blender, it exists because it is meant to efficiently wrap around a selection automatically, using Edit Poly or Edit Mesh, you can select an area to create automatically a vertex group (or use your own vertex group), which can then be used in the FFD and automatically align it to the selection.

Symmetry is also a wrapper that automatically adds a gizmo, and adds visualization for the symmetry axis selected.

For both of these modifiers, you can enable the visibility of the lattice/gizmo by toggling on/off the most left button (eye icon), the button on the right of it allows you to instantly modify the lattice/gizmo, from the same modifier panel, you’re able to go back to the object, all seamlessly.

Stack interactions

Unlike regular blender, the fact you’re capable of modifying the mesh at any point in the stack induces a slight change in philosophy, you are now able to instantly collapse the graph from a certain point (apply up to), this allows all modifiers above that point to be applied. Base mesh then becomes that applied state. This is especially important because you can now work more iteratively in the stack, meaning you can stack up modifiers to arrive to a certain mesh state. You are still able to individually apply most modifiers, but edit poly for example only allows collapsing due to them depending on upstream topology.

The addon also add modifier instancing: one modifier on several objects. You can copy one modifier (in the regular drop down menu of any modifier) and paste it to your selection (in the add modifier panel, you will see an option to paste at the bottom), either as a copy or as an instance, when that modifier is an instance, settings are fully shared, you’re able to convert the modifier as “unique” at any point which will unlink the modifier.
